messages.author: 0f88415b35482d4a
messages.subject: Areas evaluation?
parts:
Dr. Matzke,
 I'd like to ask you two questions regarding BioGeoBEARS:
 
  • I'm working with a group nearly endemic of eastern Brazil.. there is not really a good "area" scheme for this region (or at least not a single one).. Do you think that make sense to use BioGeoBEARS to test different area schemes (same number of areas, different boundaries, or even different number of areas, etc...)... that would be using the same model, same group, same phylogeny... or doesn't?
  • I'm using BioGeoBEARS 0.2.1: is everything right with the functions "bears_6param_standard_fast_ys_v" and "bears_9param_standard_fast_ys_v_cb"? The help files are the same and I guess the function also (as far as I could tell).
 
Thanks,
Marcelo

messages.author: 665b3d97beb30882
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Areas evaluation?
parts:
On 1/30/14 4:20 PM, regin...@yahoo.com.br wrote:
> Dr. Matzke,
> I'd like to ask you two questions regarding BioGeoBEARS:
>
> * I'm working with a group nearly endemic of eastern

> Brazil.. there is not really a good "area" scheme for
> this region (or at least not a single one).. Do you
> think that make sense to use BioGeoBEARS to test
> different area schemes (same number of areas, different
> boundaries, or even different number of areas,
> etc...)... that would be using the same model, same
> group, same phylogeny... or doesn't?

The difficult thing here is that likelihoods can only be
compared between different models on the *same* tip data.
Changing the definition of the geographic regions in effect
changes the geography data at the tips.

Likelihood means "probability of the data given a model",
where the "model" means "phylogeny + geographic evolution
model + model parameters".

So, using the same data, you could compare the likelihood of
the data using different trees, different geographic
evolution models, different model parameters, etc. But
changing the regions changes the data, at least in this
"discrete biogeography" way of doing things.

There may be some way around this by building a hiearchical
model, but I haven't thought about it much. Defining
"discrete regions" is very often the biggest judgment call
in these sort of analyses! When the clade lives on islands,
it's pretty simple. On continents, people often use
ecoregions, elevational zones, etc.

A number of recent biogeography papers on South America have
used about the same ecoregions, maybe you could use a subset
of those? See e.g. the Taygetis biogeography paper (google
those words to find it, I forget the reference).


What *is* feasible is to have the same areas, but have them
connected, or not, in different ways, have different
dispersal multipliers, different distances, etc., and
compare all those different models.



> * I'm using BioGeoBEARS 0.2.1: is everything right with

> the functions "bears_6param_standard_fast_ys_v" and
> "bears_9param_standard_fast_ys_v_cb"? The help files are
> the same and I guess the function also (as far as I
> could tell).

Actually, I'm going to delete those functions at some point,
they are shortcuts to some models I was playing with.
"bears_6param_standard_fast_ys_v" should work. I'm not sure
about "bears_9param_standard_fast_ys_v_cb", a model with 9
free parameters is even crazier than a model with 6!

After I wrote those functions, I came up with
bears_optim_run(), which you run with:

bears_optim_run(BioGeoBEARS_run_object)

To see the model in BioGeoBEARS_run_object, do:

BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table

You can then modify

BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table

...as you like to produce other models. Some examples of
this are in the PhyloWiki example script.


Cheers!
Nick

the method is discrete!

Nick
